title: Tenali Raman and the Midnight Sentry Parrot
summary: In a quiet lane of Vijayanagara lived an elderly scholar named Shastriji, who lived alone with an intelligent green parrot named Mithu. The parrot had learned several short phra...
keywords: the tale of the talking parrot and the thief
full_text:
In a quiet lane of Vijayanagara lived an elderly scholar named Shastriji, who lived alone with an intelligent green parrot named Mithu. The parrot had learned several short phrases from listening to the old man’s evening studies.
One night, Shastriji fell ill and was taken to the hospital, leaving his modest house empty.
Tenali Raman, being a caring neighbor, promised to watch over Shastriji’s home.

That midnight, a seasoned housebreaker named Gangu, knowing the owner was away, jimmied open the kitchen window and slipped silently into the dark house, carrying a sack to loot the brass vessels.

Tenali Raman, who was sitting quietly in the veranda shadows reading by the moonlight, heard the window creak.
Instead of rushing in with a stick, Tenali crept to the side window where the parrot’s covered cage hung near the hallway.
Tenali lightly tapped the cage and whispered in a harsh voice:
'Who is that?'

The green parrot, startled awake in the dark, immediately repeated its favorite phrase in a loud, piercing, human-like screech:
*‘WHO IS THERE? WHO GOES THERE? HALT OR I SHOOT!’*

The burglar froze in the dark kitchen, his heart leaping into his throat!
Believing an armed palace guard was standing in the shadows, Gangu whispered frantically:
'Only a poor traveler, sir! Do not shoot!'

Tenali, standing outside the lattice, rattled a heavy brass poker against an iron bucket, imitating the cocking of a musket, and whispered in a deep, menacing baritone:
'Cock the gun, brother! Take aim at his legs!'

The parrot squawked again with delight:
*‘SHOOT HIM! SHOOT HIM! FIRE!’*

Gangu dropped his loot, shrieked in absolute terror, dove out of the kitchen window, leaped over the garden wall, and ran three miles without stopping, abandoning his shoes and his burglar tools in the mud!

The next morning, Shastriji returned home to find his house intact, his brass vessels safe, and a set of valuable iron tools left behind by the fleeing thief.
Tenali Raman fed sweet figs to the green parrot, laughing at how easily a simple bird's voice and a handful of wit can defend a home better than a company of soldiers.
moral: A clear presence of mind and unexpected noise can disarm burglars without physical combat.
